title: TESS pixel centroids show that the period of half of the main-sequence M dwarfs at P < 0.2 d comes from another star; with verified rotators, contraction predicts 5.1 CPVs for 2 seen
abstract: Complex periodic variables (CPVs) are young, rapidly rotating M dwarfs with sharp dips at the rotation period. Earlier campaign results found that old main-sequence M dwarfs at the corotation-to-stellar radius ratio x of young CPV hosts have 2 CPVs where the contraction (x-only) model predicts 8.5-8.9 (p = 0.015). eROSITA data then showed that many of these short-period main-sequence stars are not X-ray saturated, which suggested that their TESS periods belong to neighbours. We tested this directly with TESS pixel data. For all 4,595 rapid rotators of the TESS 2-minute CPV samples (P = 0.08-2 d, BP-RP = 2.4-3.8) we used 8,390 light curves (up to 3 sectors per star) and found the sky position of the periodic signal from the regression of the flux-weighted centroid on the flux. Known CPV hosts give a median offset of about 2 arcsec, and 143 of 145 hosts are on target (offset <= 5 arcsec). The signal is off target (> 7 arcsec, > 3 sigma) for 14% of main-sequence rotators, but for 51% at P < 0.2 d, and for 19 of the 37 main-sequence stars at x < 3.5. Only 16 main-sequence stars at x < 3.5 are pixel-verified ultrafast rotators. eRASS1 X-ray data confirm the classes independently: the saturated fraction of main-sequence stars is 0.97 (0.94-0.99) when the signal is on target and 0.13 (0.05-0.24) when it is off target. With pixel-verified stars in training and test samples, the frozen x-only model predicts 5.1 (3.1-7.9) main-sequence CPVs for 2 observed (p = 0.14); the main-sequence rate factor at fixed x is 0.37 (0.06-1.22). Over 35 variant combinations (thresholds, error floor, best sector only, step-function and plateau-power-law x laws, X-ray weights) the prediction is 3.8-5.7 and p = 0.10-0.30. Both main-sequence CPVs are on target. The 35-750 Myr check agrees (17 seen, 15.3 predicted). Thus contraction alone is consistent with the main-sequence count, but a factor of about 0.4 is also allowed. A clean main-sequence sample 3-5 times larger is necessary to decide (power 0.83-0.98 for a factor of 0.4). Limitations: the centroid method cannot separate sources closer than about 5 arcsec; the main-sequence sample is small; the CPV labels, efficiencies and x model of the earlier publications are used without change.

Dashed and dotted lines: on-target (5 arcsec) and off-target (7 arcsec) limits. (b) Fraction of resolved stars with the signal on target against P; bars are 95% Clopper-Pearson intervals. The black line is the observed count (2). (b) Profile likelihood of a main-sequence CPV rate factor at fixed x, fitted jointly with the young training stars, without weights, with pixel-verified weights, and with pixel and X-ray weights.

citations.reason: We confirm with TESS pixel data its inference that the X-ray-quiet main-sequence rapid rotators have periods from other stars (off-target signals are X-ray quiet: saturated fraction 0.13). We reuse its X-ray likelihood code, eRASS1 query and saturated-probability model.
We repeat its frozen x-only main-sequence CPV test with pixel-verified rotators; the deficit becomes non-significant (p 0.016 to 0.14). We reuse its S1-S55 periods, CPV labels, efficiencies and code.
We reuse its stellar-parameter code and x-only rate model; with pixel-verified rotators the contraction model agrees with the main-sequence CPV count within the errors.
TESS sector 56-107 CPV survey: periods, labels, light-curve file lists, per-sector features and the centroid-source method that we extend.
BANYAN Sigma age classes and injection efficiencies.
K2 test of the contraction model that first reported the main-sequence deficit at matched x.
K2 cluster test; its plateau plus power-law x law motivates our x-law shape variants.
Dip widths of TESS CPVs in rotational phase (context for geometric explanations).
Group-held-out tests of age and corotation control of CPV rates.
